lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality, personal details that should be left off.
items.because: They are unrelated to the candidate’s qualifications.

items.says: Experience is not ordered newest-first.
items.because: Crestline appears above the more recent Harbor Payments internship.

items.says: The bullet claims late deliveries fell when the stated change was to how the rate was calculated.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments can lower the reported rate without changing when shipments arrived.

items.says: The bullet does not say what changed in the slotting rules.
items.because: Without one concrete rule change, the method behind the reduction in pick errors is hard to assess.

items.says: A first-person pronoun and passive wording obscure who implemented the redesign.
The S&OP result is not the opening bullet.
The forecast-error figures do not identify the measure used.
“S&OP” is not explained on first use.
The annual driver-hour savings do not state how they were established.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether 1,800 hours is measured or estimated or assess the basis for comparison.

items.says: The Crestline bullets cover several distinct initiatives without building a single narrative.
The 35% conversion lift does not identify its baseline or whether it means relative growth or percentage points.
items.because: Those interpretations describe different sizes of change.

items.says: The bullet does not state what dispute self-service achieved after launch.
items.because: Shipping ahead of plan does not show whether the feature created value.

items.says: The two-weeks-early delivery result is buried after the requirements and alignment details.
The annual loss estimate does not explain how six months of data were extended to a year.
items.because: The data period and estimate period differ.

items.says: The wording linking the loss estimate to the roadmap decision is cumbersome.
The line spells out “six” while using numerals for other figures.
The comparison bullet reports how the redesign was evaluated but not what the comparison found.
items.because: Without a finding, the evaluation method does not demonstrate an outcome.

items.says: The strongest onboarding result is not the opening bullet in the entry.
items.because: Starting with it would make the entry’s clearest product impact harder to miss.

items.says: The launch bullet does not show what product work or launch approach the Product Lead owned.
items.because: A reader cannot see which product decisions or launch actions were theirs.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” repeats the surplus-food idea.
items.because: The extra phrase adds length without clarifying the result.

items.says: “With two dining halls” does not make the dining halls’ role clear.
The volunteer shift system is named without explaining how it worked.
items.because: A reader cannot picture what was established to fill pickup slots and reduce staff cover.

items.says: The weekly sessions are described without stating what the practicum contributed or changed.
items.because: The bullet does not show what came out of the sessions or the value of the work.

items.says: “Held weekly working sessions” emphasizes meetings without explaining their purpose.
The shorter intake form is not linked to an outcome.
items.because: Adoption and the four-clinic scope do not show whether intake improved.

items.says: The strongest clinic-work bullet is not the opening bullet.
Passive wording in the intake and adoption clauses obscures the candidate’s role and the staff’s action.
The merchant-onboarding achievement is duplicated from the Harbor internship and does not fit the hospital-practicum work.
items.because: The same result and 2,300-merchant figure appear under Harbor Payments, leaving its ownership unclear.

items.says: “Halved the time” gives a relative change without the actual time comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how long first payment took before or after the redesign.

items.says: “It takes” uses present tense for an outcome described in the past.
items.because: The tense shift makes the phrasing less consistent and may suggest the result is ongoing.
